# Our Data

The source CSV is not included in this public repository. Place an authorized copy of `stats101b_experiment.csv` in the same folder as this file before knitting.

```{r}
dataset <- read.csv("stats101b_experiment.csv")
```

# To ensure n = 72, 9 subjects in each of 8 Sex/Caffeine/Exercise groups
```{r}
# Stats 101B
set.seed(101)

# So that we reduce from 96 to 72
trimmed_data <- c()
for (s in c("Female", "Male")) {
  for (caffeine_level in c("coffee", "decaf")) {
    for (exercise_level in c("jumping_30s", "rest")) {
      rows <- which(dataset$sex == s & 
                    dataset$caffeine_group == caffeine_level &
                    dataset$exercise_group == exercise_level)
      # Append in groups of 9
      trimmed_data <- c(trimmed_data, sample(rows, 9))
    }
  }
}

# Include all columns of attributes
dataset_final <- dataset[sort(trimmed_data), ]
dim(dataset_final)
```

```{r}
# -1 is a low level of the factor, +1 is a high level
# Easier to vectorize

# 250 mL Regular Coffee vs. Decaf
A <- ifelse(dataset_final$caffeine_group == "coffee", 1, -1)  

# Jumping for 30 seconds vs. Resting
B <- ifelse(dataset_final$exercise_group == "jumping_30s", 1, -1) 

# Sex block
blocking <- ifelse(dataset_final$sex == "Male", 1, -1)  

# Percent change in reaction time, in our dataset it was in proportion form
response <- dataset_final$proportional_change_reaction_time * 100

# So we can map -1 to Decaf/Rest and +1 to Coffee/Jumping 30 seconds
caffeine <- factor(A, levels = c(-1, 1), labels = c("Decaf", "Coffee"))
exercise <- factor(B, levels = c(-1, 1), labels = c("Rest",  "Jump 30 seconds"))

# 9 subjects per Sex x Caffeine x Exercise combination
table(dataset_final$sex, dataset_final$caffeine_group, dataset_final$exercise_group)
```

# Mean % Change per Treatment Group
```{r}
# Cell means of percent change in reaction time
cell_means <- c(
  "Decaf, Rest"  = mean(response[A == -1 & B == -1]),
  "Coffee, Rest" = mean(response[A ==  1 & B == -1]),
  "Decaf, Jump"  = mean(response[A == -1 & B ==  1]),
  "Coffee, Jump" = mean(response[A ==  1 & B ==  1])
)
 round(cell_means, 3)
```

# Why n = 72 using pwr.anova.test
```{r}
library(pwr)

# n = 19 with ceiling
pwr.anova.test(k = 4, f = 0.40, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80)

# n = 18 exactly, power rounded to nearest tenth is 0.8 
pwr.anova.test(k = 4, n = 18, f = 0.40, sig.level = 0.05)
```

# ANOVA Table
```{r}
library(phia)

# Block ANOVA
model_with_block <- aov(response ~ factor(A) * factor(B) + factor(blocking))
summary(model_with_block)
model_with_block # why we got a Sum of Squares of 1

# Puts blocks into levels, so not using this interaction plot in the report 
plot(interactionMeans(model_with_block))
```

```{r}
# Without block ANOVA
model_without_block <- aov(response ~ factor(A) * factor(B))
summary(model_without_block)
```

# Fitted Model

```{r}
regression_model <- lm(response ~ A * B + blocking)
summary(regression_model)
```

# Effect Sizes
```{r}
# Should be 2 * regression coefficients
effects <- na.omit(2 * coef(regression_model))[-1] # Exclude intercept
round(effects, 3)
```

# Interaction Plot
```{r}
# We want lines to show change from -1 to +1 level and points for endpoints, so type = "b"
# Instead of numbers, use circle and square for endpoints

interaction.plot(exercise, caffeine, response,
                 main = "Interaction Plot of Caffeine Level and Exercise Level",
                 xlab = "Exercise Level",
                 ylab = "Mean Percent Change in Reaction Time",
                 trace.label = "Caffeine Level",
                 col = c("blue", "red"), lwd = 2, type = "b", pch = c(16, 15),
                 ylim = c(-15, 5))
```

# Main Effect Plots
```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Main effect for both factors is an average
caffeine_means <- c(mean(response[A == -1]), 
                    mean(response[A == 1]))

# par() function allows x-axis to only include the levels
plot(x = c(1.1, 2.1), y = caffeine_means, type = "b", pch = 15,
     main = "Caffeine Main Effect Plot", ylim = c(-15, 5),
     xlab = "Caffeine Level", xlim = c(1, 2.3),
     ylab = "Mean % Change in Reaction Time",
     col = "brown", xaxt = "n", lwd = 4)

# Keep tick marks to show low and high level endpoints
axis(side = 1, at = c(1.1, 2.1),
     labels = c("Decaf (-1)", "Regular Coffee (+1)"))

exercise_means <- c(mean(response[B == -1]), 
                    mean(response[B == 1]))

plot(x = c(1.1, 2.1), y = exercise_means, type = "b", pch = 15, 
     main = "Exercise Main Effect Plot", ylim = c(-15, 5),
     xlab = "Exercise Level", xlim = c(1, 2.3), ylab = "Mean % Change in Reaction Time",
     col = "turquoise", xaxt = "n", lwd = 4)
axis(side = 1, at = c(1.1, 2.1), 
     labels = c("Rest (-1)", "Jump 30 seconds (+1)"))
```

# Side-by-Side Boxplot
```{r}
boxplot(response ~ caffeine + exercise,
        names = c("Decaf + Rest", "Coffee + Rest", "Decaf + Jump", "Coffee + Jump"),
        xlab = "Treatment Combination",
        ylab = "Percent Change in Reaction Time",
        main = "Side-by-Side Boxplots of Percent Change in Reaction Time",
        col  = c("red", "red", "green", "green")) # Red = rest, Green = jumping

# Treatment Means referenced around 0
abline(lty = 2, h = 0)
```

# Residual and Normal Q-Q plots
```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Residuals vs fitted: checks constant variance
# Open circles for Residual and Q-Q plots
plot(regression_model$fitted.values, regression_model$residuals,
     xlab = "Fitted Values", ylab = "Residuals",
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted")

# Need dashed horizontal line because we are using 0 as a reference residual
abline(lty = 2, h = 0)

# Normal Q-Q plot with a fitted line to identify any outliers
qqnorm(regression_model$residuals)
qqline(regression_model$residuals)
```
